stated: Labour will tackle the immediate dentistry crisis with a 'rescue plan' to provide 700,000 more urgent dental appointments and recruit new dentists in underserved areas. To rebuild dentistry long-term, they will reform the dental contract to focus on prevention and dentist retention. A supervised tooth-brushing scheme for 3- to 5-year-olds will be introduced in areas of highest need.

source.quote: Labour will tackle the immediate crisis with a rescue plan to provide 700,000 more urgent dental appointments and recruit new dentists to areas that need them most. To rebuild dentistry for the long term, Labour will reform the dental contract, with a shift to focusing on prevention and the retention of NHS dentists. We will also introduce a supervised tooth-brushing scheme for 3- to 5-year-olds, targeting the areas of highest need.

bearing_set.reason: 700,000 more urgent dental appointments, new dentist recruitment in underserved areas, contract reform, and a prevention scheme for young children all directly affect access to NHS dental care — a material healthcare access and capacity question.

Explicit targeting of 'underserved areas' for dentist recruitment and 'areas of highest need' for the tooth-brushing scheme redistributes dental provision toward deprived communities, materially bearing on O14's regional inequality and socioeconomic gap indicators.

membership_note: O3 is the primary bearing (healthcare access and capacity); O14 earns a genuine verdict because the policy is explicitly needs-weighted and geographically redistributive. O7 (early years) was considered for the tooth-brushing scheme but the intervention is a health measure, not an educational one — its effect on attainment or early-years opportunity is incidental. O2 was considered (private dental costs are a household burden) but the policy does not directly address charges, only access, so any cost-of-living relief is a secondary downstream effect, not a material O2 verdict in its own right.
